A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, and supplementary proofs. The content can be matched across reformatting and renumbering, including v1's supplementary sections and v2's Appendices A–C.

before.justification: Figure 2 and Remark SM.26 report original numerical monodromy computations of solution counts, including outcomes across six runs and certified lower bounds. These numerical results accompany the theoretical analysis.

after.justification: Figure 4 and Remark 49 retain the original numerical solution-count computations, repeated-run observations, and certified lower bounds.

M1.justification: The back-projection model, three RS1 camera types, parameter spaces, and linear and Straight-Cayley constructions are retained. The added explanations and diagrams describe the same model.

E1.justification: Both versions investigate the same minimal reconstruction problems and retain Examples 21–23. The added discussion of vehicles and scanners does not introduce evaluated datasets, domains, or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an evaluated baseline comparison against the proposed model. The prior camera models discussed in Section 1.2 remain research context; the additional citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The generic reconstruction instances, random-Jacobian minimality checks, monodromy computation procedure, and five-day interruption threshold are retained in v1 Section SM 1.6 and v2 Appendix A.6. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The Straight-Cayley cases in Examples 21–23 are unchanged. The new notation and parameter-space diagrams are explanatory displays, rather than additional case studies, ablations, or robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Remark SM.26 and Remark 49 both describe six monodromy runs, stable counts below 2000, variability for larger counts, reporting the largest observed values, and interval certification. The lower-bound and interrupted-run qualifications are unchanged.

E6.justification: All 31 solution-count entries and their qualification markers match between v1 Figure 2 and v2 Figure 4. The 34 balanced configurations, their minimality classifications, and the Straight-Cayley example findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit mathematical background, including the Grassmannian's Plücker-coordinate quadric and the definition of degree for a general projective variety. The RS1 characterization, parameter dimensions, minimal-problem theorems, and supporting proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: the rational RS1 model, camera parameterizations, line-image characterization, 31 minimal problems, and Straight-Cayley analysis. Implementing and testing practical minimal solvers remains future work.

C2.justification: The introduction adds concrete applicability discussion concerning vehicles, flatbed scanners, and pushbroom imaging. Remark 1 clarifies that reconstruction's scale ambiguity assumes no independently fixed camera scale, such as known ray distances.

D1.justification: Both supplements retain the Macaulay2 code excerpts, HomotopyContinuation.jl computation description, and references to two ancillary code files with readme.txt instructions. No substantive implementation or access-information change is documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references 32–35: work on rolling-shutter light-field reconstruction, RSL-BA, RS-NeRF, and Linear Pushbroom Cameras. These update the literature and application context while leaving Section 1.2's principal research positioning intact.

P1.justification: v2 edits and condenses passages, expands introductory motivation and mathematical background, and adds Appendix B. The main section sequence and supplementary proof organization remain recognizable, so this is a limited narrative revision.

P2.justification: The main text and supplement switch to a two-column layout with substantially reformatted mathematical displays. v2 adds Figures 2–3 and the Appendix B diagram, rearranges existing camera illustrations, and restructures the balanced-problem table.

improvement.justification: The new notation and construction diagrams, Appendix A background, and Appendix B overview make the dense geometry easier to follow. The scale qualification also improves interpretation. Some formulas become noticeably smaller in the two-column layout, but the explanatory additions provide a modest net improvement while the principal scientific results remain unchanged.
